name: Manitowoc River
blurb: Manitowoc River in Wisconsin between Wisconsin DNR-listed public accesses.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.

sections.notes: Markers identify agency-listed access; the map states whether a landing or an approximate facility area has been reviewed. Mileage is preliminary, measured along USGS river geometry; it is not a surveyed paddling route. Difficulty has not been independently rated for every section. Check current conditions, hazards and access with the managing agency before paddling.
sections.accessReview: This trip starts at the pond-ramp area above Clarks Mills Dam. A usable authorized carry from that ramp to the downstream river has not been established. Use the separately listed below-dam carry-in section instead; do not paddle over the dam.
sections.routeReview: The pond ramp and the below-dam carry-in are different access areas. This original itinerary remains withheld because its dam crossing or carry is unresolved.
sections.mapPendingReason: This trip starts at the pond-ramp area above Clarks Mills Dam. A usable authorized carry from that ramp to the downstream river has not been established. Use the separately listed below-dam carry-in section instead; do not paddle over the dam.

sections.takeOut: Lower Cato Falls County Park Carry-in
sections.difficulty: Whitewater; Class II–III at Cato Falls in agency hazard map (flow dependent)
sections.notes: A short whitewater reach from the separate below-dam carry-in to the county park landing below Lower Cato Falls. Scout the falls and confirm landing access before launching. The take-out requires a difficult steep carry; it is not a drive-up ramp. The agency water-trail plan publishes 1.2 miles for this reach. No calibrated live float-time model or trip duration is assigned.

notices.title: Seasonal park access
notices.text: Manitowoc County lists Lower Cato Falls park season as April 1–October 31, dawn to dusk. Confirm any off-season access with the county before planning this take-out.

notices.title: Whitewater and steep carry
notices.text: The regional agency hazard layer identifies Class 2–3 rapids at Lower Cato Falls, dependent on flow, and fast water with a possible strainer below Clarks Mills. These 2021 inventory observations are not a current hazard report. Scout and obtain current local guidance.
notices.sourceName: Bay-Lake Regional Planning Commission — water-trail hazards

sections.routeReview: The dotted line is an approximate agency water-trail overview starting below Clarks Mills Dam and ending below Lower Cato Falls. It passes through a whitewater reach. Exact landing approaches, usable depth and any carry around rapids are not drawn. Scout conditions and confirm the steep county-park take-out; park season is April 1–October 31.

putInAccess.operator: Managing operator not identified in the water-trail inventory
putInAccess.sourceName: City of Manitowoc GIS — Water Trail Access
putInAccess.note: Agency GIS lists this site as Existing. The2021 water-trail plan describes its public carry-in use; separate city and regional GIS records agree at the facility scale. This is an approximate access area, not a field-verified landing or assurance of present passage. Trees and steep banks limit image precision.
putInAccess.directions: Use the agency-listed carry-in on the north shore below Clarks Mills Dam, reached from County Highway J beside the bridge. This is distinct from the pond ramp above the dam. Identify the signed downstream bank approach on foot; do not launch into or paddle over the dam.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: City of Manitowoc GIS — Water Trail Access
takeOutAccess.note: Agency GIS lists this site as Existing. The2021 water-trail plan describes its public carry-in use; separate city and regional GIS records agree at the facility scale. This is an approximate access area, not a field-verified landing or assurance of present passage. Trees and steep banks limit image precision.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use the county park approach from County Highway JJ and confirm the designated river landing below Lower Cato Falls on foot. The water-trail plan describes steep slopes and a difficult carry; the county identifies stairways to the river. Park season is April 1–October 31, dawn to dusk; confirm current signs and conditions.

mapAuditNote: Access areas reviewed against current agency records. Exact water-edge landings have not been established for every endpoint; sections with unresolved permission or dam/portage questions are held separately.
